questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between the total distance travelled by a body and its displacement?

options.text: Distance is a vector quantity, whereas displacement is a scalar quantity.
Distance is the actual path length travelled, while displacement is the change in position from initial to final point in a specified direction.
Distance depends only on initial and final positions, while displacement depends on the complete path followed.
Distance can be negative, while displacement is always a positive quantity.

questions.explanation: Distance is a scalar quantity representing the complete length of the path taken during motion. Displacement is a vector quantity defined as the change in position (final position minus initial position) in a specified direction.

questions.question: Which instrument in a car measures the instantaneous speed of the vehicle at any given moment during travel?
questions.explanation: A speedometer measures the instantaneous speed of a vehicle—the speed at that precise instant in time. An odometer measures total distance.

questions.question: How is average acceleration defined in one-dimensional kinematics?

options.text: The rate of change of position per unit time
The total displacement divided by total time
The rate of change of velocity per unit time
The product of velocity and time elapsed

questions.explanation: Average acceleration is defined as the change in velocity divided by the time interval over which that change occurs (a_av = Δv / Δt).

questions.question: In the absence of air resistance, what happens to the acceleration of an object dropped near the Earth's surface during free fall?

options.text: It increases steadily as the object falls.
It remains constant at approximately 9.8 m/s² directed downwards.
It decreases to zero when the object reaches its maximum speed.
It depends directly on the mass of the falling object.

questions.explanation: In a vacuum or when air resistance is neglected, all objects fall with a constant downward acceleration due to gravity (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²), regardless of their mass.

questions.question: In a velocity-time (v-t) graph of a moving object, what physical quantity does the slope of the line represent?
questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents the acceleration of the object (Slope = Δv / Δt = a).

questions.question: A student walks 12 km North and then 16 km East in 4 hours. What are the magnitude of the average velocity and the average speed of the student for the trip?

options.text: Average velocity = 5 km/h; Average speed = 7 km/h
Average velocity = 7 km/h; Average speed = 5 km/h
Average velocity = 20 km/h; Average speed = 28 km/h
Average velocity = 5 km/h; Average speed = 5 km/h

questions.explanation: Total distance = 12 km + 16 km = 28 km. Average speed = 28 km / 4 h = 7 km/h. Resultant displacement = √(12² + 16²) = 20 km. Average velocity magnitude = 20 km / 4 h = 5 km/h.

questions.question: A car travelling along a straight road at an initial velocity of 14 m/s applies its brakes and comes to a complete stop in 5.0 seconds. What is the average acceleration of the car?
questions.explanation: Initial velocity v_i = 14 m/s, final velocity v_f = 0 m/s, time t = 5.0 s. Acceleration a = (v_f - v_i) / t = (0 - 14) / 5.0 = -2.8 m/s². The negative sign indicates deceleration.

questions.question: An object starts from rest (v_i = 0) and accelerates uniformly at 0.6 m/s² along a straight line for 4.0 seconds. What distance does it cover during these 4.0 seconds?
A ball is dropped from rest from the top of a tower. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², what is the speed of the ball after falling for 8.0 seconds, and how far has it fallen?
How can the total displacement of a moving body be determined from its velocity-time (v-t) graph?

options.text: By calculating the slope of the line
By determining the area bounded between the velocity curve and the time axis
By reading the maximum y-intercept value
By dividing the final velocity by the total time

questions.explanation: The area under the velocity-time graph bounded between the curve and the time axis represents the displacement covered by the moving object during that time interval.

questions.question: Motorcycle M travels at 120 km/h East and Car C travels at 90 km/h East on a straight parallel highway. What is the velocity of Motorcycle M relative to Car C (v_mc)?
questions.explanation: Relative velocity v_mc = v_m - v_c = 120 km/h - 90 km/h = 30 km/h in the direction of motion (East).

questions.question: A car starts from rest (v_0 = 0) and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 10 s. It then continues at constant velocity for 20 s, and finally decelerates at -4 m/s² until it stops in 5 s. What is the total distance covered by the car during the entire motion?
questions.explanation: Stage 1 (Acceleration): Top speed reached v_1 = a*t_1 = 2 * 10 = 20 m/s. Distance s_1 = 0.5 * a * t_1² = 0.5 * 2 * 100 = 100 m. Stage 2 (Constant speed): s_2 = v * t_2 = 20 * 20 = 400 m. Stage 3 (Deceleration): s_3 = v_0*t_3 + 0.5*a*t_3² = (20)(5) + 0.5(-4)(25) = 100 - 50 = 50 m. Total distance s_total = 100 + 400 + 50 = 550 m.

questions.question: A vehicle decelerates uniformly from an initial velocity of 44 m/s to 22 m/s over a time interval of 11 seconds. What is the stopping distance required for the vehicle if it continues to decelerate at this same uniform rate from 22 m/s to rest?
questions.explanation: First, find deceleration rate a = (v - v_0) / t = (22 - 44) / 11 = -2 m/s². To bring the vehicle from 22 m/s to rest (v_f = 0): v_f² = v_i² + 2*a*s => 0² = 22² + 2(-2)s => 4s = 484 => s = 121 m.

questions.question: A police officer driving at 10 m/s pursues a thief 100 m ahead who is running away at a constant velocity of 9 m/s along a straight path. How long will it take the police officer to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The relative velocity of the police officer with respect to the thief is v_pt = v_p - v_t = 10 m/s - 9 m/s = 1 m/s. Time taken to cover the initial separation of 100 m is Δt = Δs / v_pt = 100 m / 1 m/s = 100 s.

questions.question: A jet airplane (A) travels at a speed of 1000 km/h relative to the ground. It ejects hot combustion gases (B) backward at a speed of 800 km/h relative to the jet plane. What is the velocity of the hot air/gas relative to an observer on the ground?

options.text: 200 km/h in the direction of jet motion

questions.explanation: Let forward jet motion be positive (+x). Velocity of jet relative to ground v_A = +1000 km/h. Velocity of gas relative to jet v_BA = -800 km/h. Since v_BA = v_B - v_A, we get v_B = v_A + v_BA = 1000 + (-800) = +200 km/h in the direction of the jet's motion.
